title: Warehouse Management System
tagline: Know exactly what's on every shelf, in real time.
overview: A WMS replaces guesswork on the warehouse floor with a real-time system of record — every receipt, put-away, pick and pack tracked as it happens, not reconciled at the end of the day from a clipboard.
features: Guided pick, pack and ship workflows
Real-time stock visibility on the floor and in the office

process.title: Warehouse Audit
process.desc: We map your current layout, workflows and pain points before recommending any configuration.

process.title: System Configuration
process.desc: Zones, bin locations and workflows are configured to match how your warehouse actually operates.

process.title: Staff Training & Pilot
process.desc: A pilot run on one zone or shift lets staff adjust before the full switch.

process.title: Full Rollout & Support
process.desc: Full warehouse rollout with monitoring and adjustment support in the first weeks.

benefits.title: Fewer picking errors
benefits.desc: Guided, barcode-verified picking removes the most common source of shipping the wrong item.

benefits.title: Faster order turnaround
benefits.desc: Optimized pick paths and put-away logic cut the time between an order arriving and it leaving the dock.

benefits.title: Real-time stock accuracy
benefits.desc: What the system says is on the shelf is what's actually on the shelf, checked continuously rather than once a quarter.

faqs.q: Can a WMS work with our existing barcode scanners?
faqs.a: In most cases yes — we integrate with standard barcode and RFID hardware, and will flag upfront if your specific hardware needs a different approach.

faqs.q: Do we need to pause operations during rollout?
faqs.a: No — we run a pilot on one zone or shift first, so the rest of the warehouse keeps operating normally during the transition.

faqs.q: Can it handle multiple warehouse locations?
faqs.a: Yes, multi-warehouse support with per-location stock visibility is a core capability, not an add-on.

testimonial.quote: We went from a quarterly stock count nightmare to knowing our accuracy is above 99% every single day.
testimonial.author: Client Name

title: Inventory Management System
tagline: One accurate stock number, everywhere it's needed.
overview: An IMS keeps stock levels synchronized across every warehouse, storefront and marketplace you sell on, so "in stock" means the same thing everywhere — instead of three different numbers depending on which system someone checks.
features: Real-time stock sync across all sales channels
Low-stock alerts and automatic reorder points
Batch, lot and expiry date tracking
Demand forecasting based on historical sales

process.title: Stock Data Audit
process.desc: We reconcile your current stock records across every system before anything goes live.

process.title: Sync Rules Setup
process.desc: Reorder points, safety stock and sync frequency are configured around your actual sales velocity.

process.title: Multi-Channel Integration
process.desc: Every storefront and marketplace is connected so stock updates propagate in real time.

process.title: Go-Live & Monitoring
process.desc: We monitor sync accuracy closely in the first weeks and tune thresholds as needed.

benefits.title: Fewer stockouts and overselling
benefits.desc: Real-time sync across channels means you stop selling inventory you don't actually have.

benefits.title: Smarter reordering
benefits.desc: Automatic reorder points based on real velocity replace someone's gut feeling about when to reorder.

benefits.title: One number everyone trusts
benefits.desc: Warehouse staff, customer service and finance all look at the same stock figure.

faqs.q: How many sales channels can it sync with?
faqs.a: There's no hard limit — we've connected systems across a dozen simultaneous channels, from marketplaces to physical POS.

faqs.q: How fast does stock sync across channels?
faqs.a: Near real-time in most integrations, with sync frequency configurable per channel based on how each platform's API behaves.

faqs.q: Can it forecast demand or just track current stock?
faqs.a: Both — it tracks current stock in real time and uses historical sales data to suggest reorder timing and quantities.

testimonial.quote: Overselling on marketplaces was a constant headache before this. It's now something that just doesn't happen anymore.
testimonial.author: Client Name

title: Order Management System
tagline: Every order tracked from click to delivery, on one screen.
overview: An OMS pulls every order — regardless of which channel it came from — into a single dashboard, and automates the routing, splitting and status updates that used to require someone manually checking three different systems.
features: Centralized order dashboard across all channels
Automated order routing to the right warehouse
Real-time order status sync back to customers

process.title: Order Flow Mapping
process.desc: We document how orders currently move from checkout to delivery across every channel.

process.title: Routing Rules Design
process.desc: Rules for warehouse selection, splitting and prioritization are defined around your fulfillment network.

process.title: Channel Integration
process.desc: Every storefront, marketplace and payment gateway is connected into one order pipeline.

process.title: Go-Live & Optimization
process.desc: We monitor processing times post-launch and tune routing rules based on real order patterns.

benefits.title: Faster processing
benefits.desc: Automated routing means orders reach the right warehouse without a person manually assigning them.

benefits.title: Fewer fulfillment errors
benefits.desc: One source of truth for order status removes the mismatches that come from checking multiple systems.

benefits.title: Better customer communication
benefits.desc: Real-time status sync means customers get accurate delivery updates instead of a static "processing" screen.

faqs.q: Can it handle orders split across multiple warehouses?
faqs.a: Yes, split and partial shipment handling is a core feature, including separate tracking for each portion of the order.

faqs.q: Does it work with our existing payment gateway?
faqs.a: In most cases yes — we integrate with major payment gateways and will confirm compatibility with yours before starting.
Returns and exchanges run through a defined workflow that updates inventory and order status automatically once processed.

testimonial.quote: Our team used to check three tabs to answer 'where's this order.' Now it's one screen with the real answer.
testimonial.author: Client Name

title: Supply Chain Management
tagline: Visibility from supplier to shelf, without the guesswork.
overview: A supply chain management system gives you visibility into every tier of your supply network — supplier performance, procurement timing, and disruption risk — so decisions get made on current data instead of last quarter's spreadsheet.
features: Cost and lead-time analytics by supplier

process.title: Supply Chain Mapping
process.desc: We document your current suppliers, tiers and procurement processes before proposing changes.

process.title: Planning Model Setup
process.desc: Demand and supply planning models are configured around your actual lead times and seasonality.

process.title: Supplier Integration
process.desc: Key suppliers and procurement platforms are connected for real-time status and performance data.

process.title: Monitor & Optimize
process.desc: Ongoing monitoring of supplier performance and cost trends, with planning adjustments as needed.

benefits.title: Lower supply chain costs
benefits.desc: Better demand planning and supplier performance data reduce rush orders and excess safety stock.

benefits.title: Fewer disruption surprises
benefits.desc: Risk alerts flag supplier issues before they become a stockout, giving time to react.

benefits.title: Data-backed supplier decisions
benefits.desc: Supplier scorecards replace anecdotal reputation with actual delivery and quality performance.

faqs.q: Can it integrate with our current suppliers' systems?
faqs.a: Most modern supplier and procurement platforms support standard integration methods — we'll assess your specific suppliers during the mapping phase.
No, it typically works alongside your ERP, adding supply chain-specific visibility and planning that most ERPs don't cover in depth.
The system flags anomalies in supplier lead times, order confirmations and known disruption sources, so issues surface before they impact stock.

testimonial.quote: We stopped finding out about supplier delays the same week a shipment was due. Now we see it coming weeks out.
testimonial.author: Client Name

title: Transportation Management System
tagline: The right carrier, the right route, every shipment.
overview: A TMS automates the decisions that used to eat up a shipping coordinator's whole day — which carrier to use, which route to take, and how to prove delivery — while giving customers real-time tracking instead of a static tracking number.
features: Multi-carrier label printing from one screen

process.title: Shipping Profile Audit
process.desc: We review your current carriers, rates and shipping volume before recommending a configuration.

process.title: Carrier Integration
process.desc: Your existing carrier accounts are connected for live rate shopping and label generation.

process.title: Route & Rate Rules
process.desc: Rules for carrier selection and routing are configured around cost, speed and service-level needs.

process.title: Go-Live & Freight Audit
process.desc: We monitor freight spend post-launch and reconcile invoices against contracted rates.

benefits.title: Lower freight costs
benefits.desc: Automated rate shopping picks the most cost-effective carrier for each shipment instead of defaulting to one.

benefits.title: Fewer delivery disputes
benefits.desc: Proof-of-delivery capture and real-time tracking reduce "where's my package" disputes.

benefits.title: Faster label generation
benefits.desc: Multi-carrier labels print from one screen instead of switching between separate carrier portals.

faqs.q: Can we keep our existing carrier contracts?
faqs.a: Yes, the system connects to your existing carrier accounts and contracted rates rather than requiring new agreements.
Yes, including customs documentation handling for the major international carriers we integrate with.
Invoices are reconciled automatically against contracted rates, flagging discrepancies for review rather than assuming every invoice is correct.

testimonial.quote: Freight costs dropped noticeably in the first quarter just from the system picking the cheaper carrier automatically.
testimonial.author: Client Name
